findings.title: Migration crashes when embed_category site setting was never customized
findings.body: The migration does `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i`. site_settings rows only exist in the database when an admin has changed the value from the default, and embed_category defaulted to blank, so on any site that never set it this query returns zero rows. Indexing `[0]` on an empty PG::Result raises IndexError, which aborts the migration and blocks the upgrade. The same pattern is used for uncategorized_category_id on line 15. Both lookups need to tolerate an empty result.

findings.title: Migrated hosts are inserted verbatim, so entries with scheme/path or quotes break or never match
findings.body: The migration inserts each line of the old embeddable_hosts setting directly into the table with `INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)` bypassing the model. Two problems: (1) the old SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? tolerated values like 'http://example.com/page' (the old specs used such values), but the new EmbeddableHost.record_for_host matches `lower(host) = uri.host`, so a migrated host stored as 'http://example.com' will never match and embedding from that host silently stops working after the upgrade — the model's before_validation normalization never runs on migrated rows; (2) the value is interpolated into SQL unescaped, so a host containing a single quote breaks the migration (and is a SQL injection vector). The migration should normalize each host (strip scheme/path) and use bound parameters.

findings.title: Fabricator file contents were swapped between category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb
findings.body: spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb now defines `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`, while spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb defines the :category, :diff_category, :happy_category and :private_category fabricators. The fabricator definitions were placed in each other's files. Tests may still pass because Fabrication loads every file in spec/fabricators, but the filenames are now actively misleading and any tooling that maps fabricators to their expected files will break. The contents of the two files should be swapped back.

findings.title: before_validation crashes with NoMethodError when host is nil
findings.body: The before_validation callback calls `self.host.sub!(...)` unconditionally. The controller sets `host.host = params[:embeddable_host][:host]` directly, so if the host param is missing or blank, `self.host` is nil and `nil.sub!` raises NoMethodError, producing a 500 instead of a validation error. Guard with `return unless self.host.present?` (and the controller should handle a missing params[:embeddable_host] hash, which would itself raise NoMethodError on nil).

findings.title: record_for_host does not downcase the incoming host before comparing
findings.body: `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` lowercases the stored column but compares it against the raw host extracted from the referer URI. DNS names are case-insensitive and an uppercase referer host (e.g. 'HTTP://EVILTROUT.COM/...') will fail to match a stored lowercase entry, wrongly rejecting legitimate embed requests. Use `host.downcase` when building the query.

findings.title: Host validation rejects valid TLDs longer than 5 characters and there is no uniqueness constraint
findings.body: The format regex requires `\.[a-z]{2,5}` so legitimate hosts such as 'example.technology' or 'example.museum' can never be added, silently failing validation in the admin UI. Separately, there is no validates_uniqueness_of :host and no unique index in the migration, so duplicate host rows can be created; record_for_host then picks an arbitrary one (`.first`), making the effective category for that host nondeterministic.

findings.title: update/destroy raise NoMethodError (500) for a nonexistent host id
findings.body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` can return nil, and both update (via save_host, which immediately does `host.host = ...`) and destroy (`host.destroy`) dereference it. A request with a stale or invalid id returns a 500 instead of a 404. Raise RecordNotFound (e.g. use find(params[:id])) or return an error when the record is missing.

findings.title: Plural hydration can inject undefined entries when a related id is not found
findings.body: In _hydrateEmbedded, the new plural branch maps `xxx_ids` through _lookupSubType and assigns the result unconditionally (`obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []`), unlike the singular branch which only assigns `if (hydrated)`. _lookupSubType returns undefined when the id isn't present in the root payload (and for the 'category' special-case when the category isn't loaded client-side), so the hydrated array can contain undefined elements, which downstream code (e.g. `{{#each}}` rendering or .get calls) will trip over. Filter out undefined results or skip assignment when nothing resolved.

findings.title: Test 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' no longer tests what it claims
findings.body: The implementation of Topic#expandable_first_post? no longer checks whether any embeddable hosts exist (the SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? condition was removed), but this spec was kept and renamed to suggest it verifies blank-host behavior. It only passes because Fabricate.build(:topic) is unsaved so has_topic_embed? returns false — the host-blank condition is never exercised. Either the test should be removed or updated to reflect the new contract.
